transcript.text: washing machine making a horrible noise

I can certainly help you track down what's causing that noise. In washing machines, 'horrible noise' usually falls into one of three categories: violent shaking/banging (often related to installation or load balance), a deep grinding/rumbling (usually worn bearings), or a metallic ticking/scraping (a foreign object or loose part). To get us started on the right track, could you describe the noise in a bit more detail? Is it a violent shaking or banging that moves the machine, or is it a deep grinding/rumbling sound? Also, does it happen with every load (even an empty drum), or mainly with specific items like a single heavy bath mat or duvet?
It's a deep roaring rumble on the spin, like a jet engine. Happens every spin now, not just certain loads.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is drum bearings. Let's see whether the machine itself can spin: take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. Does it spin up properly when it's empty?
Yes it spins up and finishes ok, it's just really loud on the spin. Is it worth fixing? It's about 9 years old.

It depends on whether the noise is caused by a simple bearing failure or a more complex motor issue, as bearings are expensive to replace on a nine-year-old machine. If the repair cost approaches half the price of a new washer, replacement is usually the better financial choice. Washing machines refuse to spin if the load is out of balance — a single heavy item such as a bath mat, rug, duvet or a pair of jeans on its own, or a very small load, is the usual trigger. Spreading the washing out evenly or adding a few smaller items usually lets it spin. Was it a single heavy item or a very small load, or a normal mixed load?
It spins fine, it's not refusing to spin. It's a normal mixed load and the noise happens every time. So is it worth fixing or not?

It depends on the cost of the repair relative to the value of a new machine. Given the appliance is 9 years old and making severe noise, replacement is often more economical than repairing major internal components like bearings or the motor. Next, run a spin-only (or rinse and spin) programme with the washing in. Does the drum spin up properly on that programme?
Yes, it spins up fine with washing in too, I've already said that. It just roars. Can you just tell me if it's worth fixing?

It depends on the cost of the repair compared to buying a new machine. Given that the appliance is 9 years old and makes a jet-engine noise, replacement is often more economical than repairing significant internal faults like bearings or the motor. It's also worth checking the settings: wool, delicate and hand-wash programmes spin very gently, and options such as "no spin", "rinse hold" or a low spin speed stop the final spin. Was a normal programme with a normal spin speed selected, or was one of those options set?
Normal programme, normal spin speed, nothing special set. That's the third time I've said it spins fine. Is it worth fixing or not?

It depends on the cost of the repair compared to replacing the machine. Given that the appliance is about 9 years old, a major repair may not be economically viable. From what you have described, the most likely cause is foreign object / mechanical obstruction. Can you tell me whether drum stiff/jammed or only part-rotates by hand?
When I turn the drum by hand with the power off it rumbles and grinds as it turns. It's not stuck though. Is it worth fixing?

It depends on the cost of replacing the bearings or drum assembly compared to buying a new machine. Given the appliance is 9 years old and the noise indicates significant internal wear, replacement might be more economical than repair. From what you have described, the most likely cause is drum bearings. A washing machine won't run if the door lock doesn't engage. Close the door firmly, check nothing like a sock or the seal is caught in it, and start a programme. Does the door click locked and the lock light come on?

candidates: Transit bolts/brackets still fitted (if new/recently moved) (medium)
Worn suspension (shock absorbers/springs) or drum bearings (low)
plan: The fault they reported is: "making a horrible noise". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
